A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Superficial Safety Alignment Hypothesis. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material and identifying removed plots.

before.justification: v2 reports original probing, pruning, fine-tuning and alignment experiments in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds empirical comparisons with safety-unit freezing baselines in Appendix A.2, Tables 7–10.

M1.justification: The importance scoring, four unit categories, SCU/CU freezing and RU-only fine-tuning procedures remain unchanged. Appendix A.2's maximal-set explanation elaborates the existing selection procedure; additional freezing ratios are experimental configurations.

E1.justification: The added comparisons reuse Alpaca/GSM8K fine-tuning and AdvBench/HEx-PHI evaluation, all already present in v2. Existing instruction-following, utility and HarmBench jailbreak coverage is retained. The new baseline's Wikipedia calibration choice does not introduce a new target task or evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained full-fine-tuning and PEFT comparisons, v3 evaluates Zhao et al. (2025)'s neuron/channel freezing and Li et al. (2024b)'s safety-layer freezing in Tables 7–10. These add directly relevant safety-preservation comparators; the other methods summarized in Table 6 are literature comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 introduces controls for the new comparisons: shared safety attribution data, Wikipedia calibration for Zhao's foundation neurons, 0.4% and 6.3% selection variants, and a matched 28.1% frozen-parameter budget against Li's blocks 6–14. Previously reported experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a larger-budget Zhao variant that tests sensitivity to neuron selection size. It removes v2 Figures 13–15, which analyze alignment transfers across individual blocks. The pruning ablations, CU freezing-ratio sweep, jailbreak tests and aggregate transfer analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose seed 42 for probe-model training. There are no added repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or changes to uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Tables 7–10 add comparative safety results and results for the proposed method at the new matched budget. For example, Table 9 reports Alpaca HEx-PHI/Llama3-Guard ASR of 8.18% for the proposed method versus 12.12% for Li et al. with 28.1% frozen. Existing Tables 1–5 retain their values; v2's blockwise results in Figures 13–15 are removed.

T1.justification: Equation 1, importance-score standardization and the mathematical setup are unchanged. Replacing 'corollary' with 'implication' and explaining maximal versus minimal safety-unit sets do not add formal results, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims about binary safety decisions, small safety-critical subsets, safety preservation through freezing, and redundant units as an alignment budget. The new comparisons support these retained contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 explains the new baseline advantages through maximal versus minimal safety-unit selection and finer granularity. Appendix A.1 adds a caveat about applicability to backdoor attacks. Conversely, v2 Section 5's explicit limitation to SFT on limited alignment datasets is removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-website pointer for code implementation and documents the new baselines' calibration sources, selection ratios and frozen block range. The previously disclosed hardware, optimizer, training parameters and data splits remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands positioning across safety-unit manipulation, data/task-distribution explanations and optimization-based defenses, supported by Table 6 and numerous added references. It presents the interventions primarily as mechanistic tests of SSAH. Some earlier bibliography entries, including ALERT and Mistral 7B, are removed.

P1.justification: Most retained prose and section ordering remain intact. Changes include conference headers, removal of the opening warning and revision note, 'corollary' becoming 'implication', a streamlined conclusion, and insertion of Appendix A with corresponding appendix renumbering.

P2.justification: v3 adds a qualitative comparison matrix and four empirical comparison tables, removes three block-transfer plots, and relocates several retained displays, including Figure 1 to the first page. v2 Figure 16 is retained as v3 Figure 13, rather than replaced by a new analysis.

improvement.justification: The directly relevant freezing baselines, especially the matched-budget comparison, improve assessment of the intervention beyond v2's full-fine-tuning and PEFT comparisons. The expanded research positioning also clarifies its contribution. These gains are tempered by removal of the explicit SFT/dataset limitation and three block-level analyses; the central hypothesis evidence and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.
